text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me, love?
B: Yes, I hear you. Hello, I'm Rasa.
A: Nicola. Nice to meet you. How are you doing today?
B: I'm okay, thank you. Bit tired. And you?
A: Oh, same, I'm always a bit tired, don't worry. Where are you?
B: Leyton, East London.
A: I'm St Helens, up near Liverpool. I'll be honest, when I saw your photo I thought, she looks like a busy mum like me. Nice tidy kitchen, mind. Mine's a tip.
B: Ha, it's tidy only for the photo. I thought same about you, tired mum. How many kids?
A: Two. Ellie's fifteen and Jake's twelve. You?
B: One. Emilija, she is twelve. Year 8.
A: Same as Jake! Are they driving you mad yet? Jake's football boots already don't fit him, I only bought them in September.
B: Yes, the shoes. And the school, always they want money for something. Now is some project, we have to buy another thing. Every week another thing.
A: Oh, tell me about it. And everything's gone up. I do most of mine at Aldi and the reduced shelf, and even that's dear now.
B: Lidl for me. Prices are crazy, yeah. Do you work?
A: Not at the minute, no. I've got rheumatoid arthritis, so I've been off sick about four years. I used to be a carer in a residential home. Ellie does a lot of the shopping now, bless her, and some of the cooking. She did a Thai green curry from TikTok last week and it was actually lovely.
B: Oh, that's nice she helps. Thai curry, it's spicy, no?
A: A bit, yeah. Are you not a spice person?
B: No, not really. I'm Lithuanian, we eat potatoes, potatoes, more potatoes. At weekend I made cepelinai, it takes all afternoon.
A: What's cepelinai, then? Sorry, have I said that right?
B: Yes, close. It's like big potato dumpling, with meat inside, and you put sour cream and bacon on top. Shape like a zeppelin, that's why the name. My daughter loves it, my husband loves it, I'm knackered after.
A: Oh, that sounds right up my street. We do scouse when it's cold, which is sort of the same idea, meat and potato and you're full till next week.
B: Scouse is what?
A: It's a stew, lamb or beef with potatoes and carrots, cooked for ages. Liverpool thing. You have it with red cabbage and bread. Do you cook every night?
B: Most nights, yes. I make dinner, if I'm tired then pasta. I work in bakery, so we always have bread, I bring home what's left.
A: Free bread! I'd be made up with that. Do you go back to Lithuania much?
B: Every summer, two or three weeks. My mum is there alone, so I worry a bit. We speak on video every Sunday.
A: Ah, that's nice you do that. My mum died two years ago and I still go to ring her sometimes, do you know what I mean? So keep doing your Sundays.
B: Yes. I'm sorry about your mum.
A: Thank you, love. Anyway, I'm waffling, sorry. I think we're nearly done.
B: Yeah, it was nice to talk to you, Nicola.
A: You too, Rasa. Enjoy your cepelinai.
